title: Protocol to isolate human normal and neoplastic pancreatic cells for single-cell omic analyses
protocol: Cut away a piece of pancreatic tissue by a qualified pathologist.
Remove any blood, fascia, necrotic or scorched areas from the tissue.
Place the tissue in approximately 10 mL of Preservation Buffer in a 50-mL tube and transport it on ice to the laboratory within 30 min.
Transfer the tissue to a 50-mL tube and add approximately 10 mL of cold 1×PBS.
Gently invert the tube several times.
Repeat step to wash off any residual blood and pancreatic enzymes twice.
Transfer the tissue to a 5-mL conical tube and add approximately 1 mL of solution.
Using sterile ophthalmic straight scissors, mince the tissue on ice into tiny pieces smaller than 1 mm × 1 mm within 5 minutes.
Transfer the minced tissue mixture to a 100 mm × 20 mm round culture dish using a sterile Pasteur pipette.
Add enough digestion buffer to reach a maximum volume of 10 ml for normal human pancreas.
For neoplastic human pancreas, transfer the minced tissue mixture to a 50-mL tube and add enough digestion buffer to reach a maximum volume of 15 ml.
Incubate the mixture in a 100 mm × 20 mm round culture dish at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Pipette the mixture gently about 20 times.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for another 5 minutes.
Examine the tissue's dissociation state microscopically before each new incubation.
Transfer the mixture to a new 50-mL tube after incubation.
Let the mixture stand for 30 seconds until tissue pieces settle down.
Filter the supernatant through a 40-μm strainer into another tube.
Transfer the dissociated mixture into a 50-mL tube and allow it to settle until all tissue pieces settle down.
Transfer the supernatant from the old tube (tube i) into a new tube (tube ii).
Filter the supernatant with a 40-μm strainer, leaving visible undissociated tissues behind.
Resuspend the sediment with 10 mL Digestion Buffer and transfer the mixture into a new 100 mm × 20 mm round culture dish for another round of dissociation steps until the fourth time.
Incubate the mixture in a 50-mL tube at 37°C for 5 min at a shaking speed of 50 rpm.
Gently pipette the mixture with a clean Pasteur pipette about 20 times and incubate for another 5 min under the same conditions.
Pipette the minced tissue gently in Digestion Buffer to disperse the mass and facilitate further dissociation.
Pipette again to reinforce the effect of dispersing the tissue mass.
Incubate the mixture for 20 minutes at 37°C with shaking at 50 r.p.m.
Gently pipette the solution after incubation, let it stand for 30 seconds until most tissue pieces settle down.
Filter the supernatant through a 40-μm strainer and keep the filtrate on ice.
Resuspend the sediment with 15 ml Digestion Buffer and continue incubating at 37°C for 30 minutes with shaking at 50 r.p.m.
Filter the mixture again through a 40-μm strainer after incubation.
Collect the filtrates from the previous steps.
Centrifuge the filtrate at 800 × g for 4 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in at least 5 mL freshly prepared Lysis Buffer and incubate at room temperature for 5 min, avoiding light.
Transfer the suspension into a 15-mL tube, centrifuge it at 800 × g for 4 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet with 1 mL Wash Buffer.
Transfer the suspension into a new clean 15-mL tube using wide-bore pipette tips.
Add excess 4 mL Wash Buffer to the suspension in the new tube.
Centrifuge the suspension at 600 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant from the centrifuged suspension.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL Wash Buffer using wide-bore pipette tips and transfer it into a new clean 15-mL tube.
Add excess 4 mL Wash Buffer to the resuspended pellet in the new tube.
Centrifuge the suspension at 400 × g for 6 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant from the centrifuged suspension.
Resuspend the pellet with an appropriate volume (40–200 μL) of Wash Buffer using wide-bore pipette tips.
Mix 10 μL of the cell suspension with 10 μL of 0.4% Trypan blue stain.
Assess the viability and concentration of cells using Countess II and microscopy.
Dilute the single-cell suspension to the required concentration by adding an appropriate volume of Wash Buffer based on the initial cell concentration.
